gaps.sentence: The scheme is costly; on the ___ hand, it would create hundreds of jobs.
gaps.explanation: 'On the other hand' balances a drawback against an advantage.

gaps.sentence: Please complete the form in block capitals ___ it can be read easily.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces a clause with subject and modal; so as to/in order to need an infinitive.

gaps.sentence: ___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.

gaps.sentence: Far from resenting the changes, the staff welcomed them; ___, productivity rose.
gaps.explanation: Rising productivity is an additional point in the same direction: moreover.

gaps.sentence: The delegates arrived early ___ have time to network.
gaps.explanation: 'So as to + infinitive' = in order to, a formal purpose linker.

gaps.sentence: He went back inside, ___ the danger.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the danger' — noun phrase; although needs a clause.

gaps.sentence: Take a jumper ___ the evening turns cold.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution against possibility.

gaps.sentence: He passed the oral exam ___ the fact that he had barely revised.
gaps.explanation: 'The fact that' turns the clause into a noun phrase, which 'despite' requires.
